preview.pick: Agents that dissolved most readily in water were the ones that could be given to an animal in the smallest doses

served.stem: According to the passage, what did Meyer and Overton find when they compared the anaesthetic agents available in their day?
choices: Agents that dissolved most readily in water were the ones that could be given to an animal in the smallest doses
How readily an agent dissolved in olive oil predicted how little of it was needed to anaesthetize an animal
Heavier molecules were consistently more potent than lighter ones
Every agent worked by binding the same receptor in the nerve membrane
The agents varied so widely that no single ordering of them could be found
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 2 states it directly: ranking the agents by how readily each dissolves in olive oil predicts almost exactly how little of each is needed. The measurement was solubility in oil, and the finding was a prediction of potency.

proof.quote: how readily each dissolves in olive oil, that ranking predicts almost exactly how little

passage.title: Why Anaesthesia Still Lacks an Explanation

distractorNotes: The passage names olive oil, not water, and it later calls these molecules reluctant to stay dissolved in water.
Molecular weight never enters the comparison; the only property measured was solubility.
The lipid account that grew out of the finding was attractive precisely because it needed no receptor at all.
The opposite is stated. The ranking held across more than four orders of magnitude of potency.

answer.text: How readily an agent dissolved in olive oil predicted how little of it was needed to anaesthetize an animal
answer.line: Paragraph 2: rank the agents by how readily each dissolves in olive oil, and that ranking predicts how little of each is needed.

steps: Find the names. Meyer and Overton open paragraph 2.
Read the whole finding. They ranked agents by how readily each dissolves in olive oil, and the ranking predicted how little of each puts an animal under.
Use sentence 2 as a filter: one ranking held across more than four orders of magnitude. Any choice where no order holds is out.

choices.note: The ranking was by oil. The potent agents dissolve greedily in oil, and paragraph 8 calls them reluctant to stay dissolved in water.

choices.note: Paragraph 2, sentence 1, nearly word for word: oil solubility predicts the dose needed.

choices.text: Heavier molecules were consistently more potent than lighter ones
choices.note: Molecular weight never enters paragraph 2. The one property measured was how readily each agent dissolves in oil.

choices.text: Every agent worked by binding the same receptor in the nerve membrane
choices.note: Their finding was read as pointing at the oily membrane. The account built on it ends: one site, one mechanism, no receptors required.

choices.text: The agents varied so widely that no single ordering of them could be found
choices.note: Sentence 2 says the opposite: one ranking held across more than four orders of magnitude of potency.
